projectSummary: Within-participant acute surface-EMG comparison of five bench inclinations (0, 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees) at 60 per cent of one-repetition maximum in 30 trained adults, with the pectoralis major resolved into upper, middle and lower portions.

publication.statusSource: NCBI PubMed and PMC records fetched 2026-09-13; no retraction or correction notice

notes: Surface EMG is an acute activation measure and is not evidence of hypertrophy.
Portion assignment is by electrode site over the upper, middle and lower pectoralis major; it is a regional sampling of one muscle, not an independently validated compartment boundary.

This record is one of the two studies R1 finding I-13 identified as absent from the first pass and contradicting the inclination claim as it was then worded. It entered screening here through the amended portion-terminology stratum N-RS4a.
The relationship across bench angle is non-monotonic and reverses above 45 degrees, which is inside the range the first-pass claim asserted.

study.population: Thirty trained adults performed the bench press at 0, 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees of bench inclination at 60 per cent of one-repetition maximum, with surface EMG recorded from the upper, middle and lower portions of the pectoralis major, the anterior deltoid and the medial head of the triceps brachii.

title: Effect of Five Bench Inclinations on the Electromyographic Activity of the Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, and Triceps Brachii during the Bench Press Exercise
